messages:
carmen: hi all, i'm carmen — just joined runtime team today. following the README to build from source on Ubuntu 22.04 with CUDA 12.2. build fails at link with a cublasLt symbol error. any onboarding tips? :wave:

ryan: welcome carmen! short checklist: nvcc --version, nvidia-smi, and `ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublasLt.so*`. also are you using the distro cuda packages or the NVIDIA runfile?

carmen: nvcc shows 12.2.148, nvidia-smi driver 525.something, and there is a libcublasLt.so.12 in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu. build log snippet:
```
/usr/bin/ld: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublasLt.so.12: undefined reference to `cublasLtMatmulDescCreate'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

nina: that usually points to driver/runtime mismatch or a stale library from distro packages. we recommend driver 535+ for CUDA 12.2 in our docs. are you on a company machine or personal laptop?

carmen: personal laptop; hesitant to reinstall drivers. is there a less invasive workaround?

ryan: you can use the dev container `ghcr.io/redwood-inference/rt-dev:cuda12.2` which isolates the toolchain. locally, try setting LD_LIBRARY_PATH to point to the CUDA install first: `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH` then `make clean && make -j`. also run `ldconfig -p | grep cublasLt` to see which file the linker resolves.

nina: also check `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/` for leftover vendor paths. if the linker resolves to a libcublasLt from the distro that doesn't match nvcc, you'll see symbols missing. the cleanest is the docker image or a VM.

carmen: ran ldconfig -p, it points to /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublasLt.so.12. i tried LD_LIBRARY_PATH but linker still prefers /usr/lib.

ryan: try `gcc -Wl,-verbose` during link to view search order, or add `-Wl,-rpath,/usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64` to the link flags in your local build (quick test). if that fixes it we can add a note to the onboarding doc.

infra-bot: Heads-up: recommended image ghcr.io/redwood-inference/rt-dev:cuda12.2 available. Use for onboarding to avoid host conflicts.

carmen: thanks — i'll try the container for now and open a tiny docs PR suggesting rpath note and driver matrix. who owns runtime onboarding docs?

nina: runtime infra owns it (cc @ryan). please tag me on the PR and i'll review. welcome aboard! :tada:
